release.headline: Subshell 1.0.5: swipes that act when you let go, and Reddit's own reasons when a post is refused
highlights: Swipes: a vote or other swipe action now runs the moment you let go, and the post or comment springs straight back instead of sliding off the screen.
Swipes: pick a swipe distance in Settings › Navigation & gestures and try it on a card there. Standard is a little longer than before; Short is the old distance.
Posting: when Reddit refuses a post or comment, the notice says why in Reddit's own words, for example a community's minimum length, and scrolls into view.
Posting: a community's own posting rules, such as a word the title must contain, are shown on the field they apply to.
Wiki: pages show when they were last edited, and that edits made in Reddit's new Wiki may not have reached apps.
Behind the scenes: newer Android libraries (Compose 1.13, Material 3 1.5).
If something does not work for you, tell us on r/subshell or GitHub.
